Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab Fisher-Price Imaginext toys in general are great toys. Durable, bright colored plastic that often take after popular shows and movies such as Batman and Superman, Power Rangers, or in this case, Jurassic World. These toys have allowed my son's imagination to run wild and be creative as he plays for many hours with these. We often play together, but for the most part he's very happy to play with these on his own for hours at a time. I probably purchased my first Imaginext toy about 3 years ago, Batman and his Batcycle. It has held up to the test of time and a very rough preschooler. My son is now 6 with multiple sets.

Jurassic World has been all the rage in my house this summer because little boys love dinosaurs and that is certainly true of mine! So, take his love for Imaginext toys and mix that with his love for dinos and it's the perfect mashup! The only caveat is that on Amazon I have found the prices to vary greatly from in stores. Toys R Us (R.I.P.) was a great source for Imaginext because they always had the best and lowest price on these. They also had more selections. So, I would caution anyone to first look around Target or Walmart first. I once bought Batgirl and her Batcopter for $30 on Amazon and it was in Toys R Us for $15. I regularly see Imaginext toys in Target selling for $5-10 cheaper than on Amazon.

With the Fisher Price Imaginext Jurassic World Research Lab you get one T-Rex, one scientist, one harpoon, and one claw. There is a "decontamination" chamber for the scientist to get clean to study his subject. Simply turn the powerpad and the blue decontamination spiral gets the scientist ready. There is a powerpad to open and close the cage for the T-Rex. But watch out! The T-Rex might get loose! the lab is not that big. It's smaller than all of the Batcaves I've ever purchased. It's no bigger than any of the Paw Patrol sets I've purchased as well. So, it's east to tuck it away in a corner. All of the pieces, including the T-Rex, we've placed in a plastic show box for organization and storage. Overall, it's a fun play-set that provides hours of entertainment and keeps kids away from screens!
text_fidelity_b: Jurassic World Toys , Research Lab

text_fidelity_a:
Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Short version of the review: it’s a fun game with a pretty good first-game learning curve that settles in pretty quickly in subsequent games. It can be long (though you can adjust it). We’ll add it to our rotation of “lengthy” games

Longer version

1) Packing
I’m going to ding the game for packaging because while everything comes fine (as is typical, there’s a lot of popping pieces out of their cardboard sheets), I like when games include easy ways of keeping thing together and/or organized once you’ve played the first game. Even if it’s as minimal as separate small plastic bags. We used our own tiny bags (we’ve learned to keep ones that do come with other games if they’re extra thanks to consolidation) and a few regular small baggies, but I don’t think it’s too much to ask that those things be included

2) Materials
All the materials seem of good quality. Cards are not super-thick but they’re not at all flimsy, the non-plastic pieces feel solid and you don’t have any sense that they’ll start coming apart or getting dented/torn. The plastic cities are a nice touch, but the capital cities could perhaps have been made a little more distinctive. Not at all a big deal; a close look is all you need.

3) Instructions
The big sheet of instructions is fine. Generally clear and well written, with a few “clarification” points at the end, which is a nice touch. We had a few questions that weren’t included, but they were easy to find online. A few individual player cards with a stripped down bit of instruction for quick, easy reference would have been nice to toss in

4) Set up
As noted (and as is usual for these types of games) there’s a lot of popping things out and organizing. Once that’s done the first time, set-up is relatively quick. You put together some map tiles which is easy enough (though this 50+-year-old wouldn’t have minded if the organizing numbers were a little bigger on each tile). Each player gets tokens, a set of cards five of which are laid out in a particular order under their “Focus” bar (the cards are in these areas: Military, Technology, Culture, Economy, Industry), a set of “diplomacy” cards, a “leader” card (who they “play”—Cleopatra for instance), a few caravans (little wagons used for trading). After you’ve done it a few times it’s a pretty quick set-up. You also set up some cards to the side of the play area (World Wonder cards and City-State Diplomacy Cards and Victory Cards (these are what determine how the game is won). This is always an issue in these sorts of game because of course they’re not going to be truly “visible” to all the players. Someone is going to have to move or ask to see them to see what they say (some change throughout the game). I have no idea how to get around that though; it’s just a matter of physical setting.

5) game play
I’m not going to detail it. But generally, the Victory cards have two “agendas” on them, such as build two Wonders of the World, and a player who achieves one agenda from each of the cards is the winner (this is nice because you can shorten the game if desired by simply playing with fewer Victory cards). As far as the play itself
1) Players can “resolve” (do what it says) any one of the five cards below their Focus bar. This might mean building a city, attacking someone, moving a caravan, laying out a “Control” piece to claim a hex space (i.e. territory).
2) Once they’ve done that, that card gets move to slot one under the bar and all the others move one slot to the right. This is key because the slot number affects how the card is resolved. For instance, when you attack using your military card, you roll a die and add the slot number (and possibly other bonuses) to your roll. So you’re going to want to attack when that card is in the 4 or 5 position typically, not the 1 or 2 slot. This adds a nice bit of complexity to your action choices.

That’s pretty much the gameplay for players. A few other factor include
1) You can swap out a card under your focus by advancing your “Tech” counter a certain number (you do that using one of the cards). Once you hit a certain level, you can exchange one low level card for one that’s a bit more powerful. There are 4 levels of cards.
2) Barbarian tokens on the board move at regular periods and they can end up destroying one of your caravans or claiming territory from you (which affects how much money your cities earn and how much you can advance)
3) Caravans allow you to gain trade tokens that can be used to increase the impact of your cards. For example, if you have two trade tokens on your military card, you can spend one or both to add a bonus to your roll. Caravans can also garner you another player’s Diplomacy card, which has certain benefits dependent on the card.
4) Placing a control tokens mean you’ve claimed territory (that particular space), which is necessary for collecting trade tokens (a “mature” city garners you a set number of trade tokens once you’ve “controlled” all adjacent tiles), collecting resources such as marble or diamonds, or for building cities (your build cities a certain number of spaces from a space you’ve controlled with a token).
5) The terrain has an impact on your choices. In order of scaled “easiness”, the terrains are 1-grasslands, 2-hills, 3-forest, 4-desert, and 5-mountains. To travel through a desert is considered difficult, so that 4 means your Economy card (the one that moves your caravan) needs to be in the 4 or 5 slot. Similary, to build a city in a mountain space means your Industry card has to be in the 5 slot.

There are more rules and factors that come into play, but that’s the general gist. As noted at the start, I’d say the learning curve is relatively steep the first time ( a lot of going back to the instruction booklet), but past the first game or two, it comes pretty easily. I’ve certainly played games with a far steeper curve and one that takes longer to get to know game play well. If I were ranking learning curves on a ten-point scale, I’d probably put this around a 6.

Turns move slowly the first time or two as people try to remember what they can do, what they need to do, etc. But after the first hour each player moves pretty quickly through their turns as you’ve gotten used to how to deal with the complexities of those shifting slots under the Focus bar. As people get closer to each other, things slow again as players try and figure out cost-benefit of attacking, but then as before, after a few attacks those move quickly.

I liked the game quite a bit. More than my two family members, but I tend to have more patience for the slowness of things and I mind long game less than they do. They did like it enough to play again. And as mentioned, I like that you can self-adjust your length simply by cutting out one of the agendas. It’s a game we’ll definitely keep and keep playing.
text_fidelity_b: Civilization A New Dawn Board Game | Tactical Strategy Game for Adults and Teens Based on the Hit Video Game Series | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

It’s not like a lot of the other games out there - which makes it really neat.
The game is easy to play once you get started - its a little confusing at first but makes sense once the first player has gone.
If I could change anything about the game it would be:
- That the game board was thicker and bigger - it would be better if they had a regular style board thickness that folded in half even. This would allow the cupcakes to fit in the center easier and when little hands knock the pile over it doesn’t make such a mess of the board.
- That the tea pot arrived assembled and all the stickers attached. Once the teapot is assembled it no longer fits into the box which is SUPER ANNOYING!!! When games come with stickers and they aren’t already attached my kids want to do it! Then they get mad when they are not on straight. Then they get mad when they removed the sticker to straighten it and it no longer sticks.
I really do love the game and thinks its fun. I love how the dice come out of the tea pot to reveal the space count and number of cupcake cards.
I think its a little silly to keep the cupcake card and get a stack of sugar cubes when you have a match. Just one of those would have been fine. We tend to just toss the cupcake back in the pile and just put the sugar cube in the cup - it’s less to keep track of!

Large 2.5LB Professional Rock Tumbler Kit, 3-Speed Motor & 9-Day Timer, Rubber Barrel, Quiet Rotary Stone Polisher with 5 Belts, Rough Gemstones, 4 Polishing Grits, for Adults Kids (Black) My kids have recently shown interest in gems and geology, so they were super excited to try this out! This is a full kit, which means it comes with everything you need: Not only the tumbler parts, but also the various stage mixes and even the raw rocks to use!
I actually was hoping it was the sort of thing we could use more than once, learn how to use it with the included stuff and then do more of our own found rocks with the next batch! The thing is, it comes with only enough to do the included rocks, and you have to do them all at once if you want them to come out with the included materials. Beyond that, you can reuse the machine but you have to get more materials to put in with the rocks.
The machine also takes a LONG time. I knew tumbling was a process, but it's a few stages and each one takes a few days, so the whole thing took weeks of emptying out and putting in the next stage and setting the timer for the next set of days spinning. text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

Activity tables, in general, have always been a huge hit with all of our babies, but this one is more unique in the sense that it encourages a lot of pounding. text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

I collect them so I saved everything. If you set him on a flat surface he rocks so it's best to keep him in his shell for extra stability and cuteness factor.😍

HATCHING::
The process takes about 20 minutes and you get to encourage him on his journey. He responds with adorable sounds to show you he is trying his hardest to meet you. His eyes flash and he makes grunting and light struggling sounds. 😍

A DRAGON IS BORN: 🐣
Toothless greets you with cooing with flapping wings, head tilts, and happy sounds.🐥

PLAYING:
He has 7 settings and play modes with 4 touch sensors and responds with different actions and sounds depending upon which sensor is activated by touch. Toothless is equipped with a mic and reacts to voice. Place his fish near his mouth and he makes eating sounds, but his mouth doesn't open or close. In blast mode, there are two blue LED lights on each side of his mouth that flash and he makes a photon blast power-up sound. He makes several sounds (I haven't counted them all yet) with affectionate noises to encourage interaction. ❤️

Overall Toothless is a MUST HAVE for anyone who enjoys robotic toys. I would have been over the moon💗🌙 if this were available when I was growing up and I don't know of any child who would not enjoy him. I certainly do. I would rate him at 4 1/2 stars due to the price. This is a well thought out and high-quality toy. I absolutely adore him 😍, but he lacks some of the more sophisticated programming and functionality of my other animatronic robotic pets. I still highly recommend him because he is cute and unique. If you saw the movie you'll love and enjoy him all the more.

Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set We hold a monthly “Game Night” at our house and felt this was the perfect opportunity to introduce the Pathfinder Card game to our friends. Unfortunately, it took at least two hours to explain the rules of the game and our crowd is mostly people over 40, so keeping track of each character’s journey, remembering what powers they do or do not have, and explaining strategy was somewhat difficult, especially as everyone was a first time player. I think this game is best suited to a younger crowd (under 40) but it’s still fun for those who really stick with it.

A few of us played Dungeons & Dragons years ago, so this playing this felt very familiar. Every player is given the opportunity to "customize" their game play, in that they can choose to be a particular character. The characters are individually possessed of different powers, spells, weapons, and capabilities. You choose a specific character and a “scenerio” (a.k.a storyline) and draw cards that determine the path of your journey. Your objective is to maximize your advantage, using the cards and dice to advance or retreat. The objective, of course, is to win the game by overcoming monsters and capturing the bad guys for points. It’s like a video game in that they are different levels and you can move on to different stages. The game shifts scenes as you advance, so it feels like a continual maze. The game can technically go on forever as the company encourages you to buy “expansion sets” that give you additional cards and new adventures to go on.

Two people in our group are big science fiction and fantasy buffs, and they absolutely loved it. For the rest of us, it was challenging, and after playing this for two hours, a little tedious, since it requires so much thinking. This is not a game to be played when you’ve had a few cocktails! This toy set, on the positive side, does have very attractive, bright colors, and it does inspire creative play, as the older, wooden sets did. It's just not wood!

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game I am a board game afficionado. I own over 200 different strategy, social or silly games, and you'd better believe that my daughter is a gamer in waiting. Of course, as a young boy, Pretty Pretty Princess wasn't on my radar for myself, but I knew the name and the concept, and when it was my time to find a copy for my kid, there's no way I was paying the multiple hundreds for the original 80's item.

So I was thrilled when an appropriately priced remake made it's way to my house, and all it took was reading the name to hook my daughter (and interestingly, my wife as well) into a quest to become the most beautiful in all the realm.

The box for this one opens upside down for some reason, and one you get inside, you'll find a spinner, an odd, nearly blank game board, and some teeny tiny jewels to bling out your ensemble. Play is simple - you spin the spinner, attempt to move aroudn the circular board to earn all your gems, and the first one to get everything is crowned (literally) the prettiest princess.

Perhaps the most striking thing is the lack of effort they put into the board and spinner. Both are of reasonable thickness and sturdy, but there is almost nothing on the board in terms of graphic design outside of the logo on the field of white, and the spinner is literally numbers. They may have changed the font away from Times New Roman, but that's all there is to it. It looks like a high school kid's graphic design project, and not one that's going to earn high marks from the teacher.

That said, it's good to have this game back in print again, even if the game play is not particularly solid, and even if the graphics leave quite a bit to be desired. As I said, all I needed to do to get my little one to play was to tell her the name of the game, and my wife jumped right in on the nostalgia boat as well.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game

I showed my kids videos of cable cars and some of the old department stores in San Francisco that I remember going to as a child with my dad, where we would dress up fancy for the event.

We have the grand department store, the delicious restaurant, and the grocery store from calico critters, and the kids just love playing with all of the different pieces and acting out purchasing things, eating special foods, trying on clothes, etc. And how do we get there? We have both a blue vehicle for calico critters derided, and also this cool ride along tram.

The tram just feels special, new, and different. The critters can all hang out together and go for a special ride, and sometimes they even take a long action figures, Lego figures, and other unrelated toys. I haven't seen any other cars for toys to ride in that are as elegantly and creatively built as this one. The kids love it and it has been played with for six months with absolutely no sign of damage or wear.
text_fidelity_b: Calico Critters Town Ride Along Tram

Bgraamiens Puzzle-Blooming Color-1000 Pieces Color Challenge Blue Board Round Jigsaw Puzzles I just completed this puzzle, and have some pro's and con's to share:

Pro's: It's very pretty and big.
Pieces are appropriately thick for a 1,000 piece puzzle
Pieces are printed on the back with "A", "B", "C", "D". If you sort by letter, you will have all the pieces to do
1/4 of the puzzle. Great idea if your table space is limited, or if more than one person is working on it.
If you want greater difficulty, don't look at the back!
Storage box is good quality cardboard.

Con's: About 20% of the pieces were not cut through, so I had to tear them apart, causing damage to some of
the backs.
One piece was missing, and there was an extra edge piece. Based on other reviews, I won't bother trying
to contact the seller because no one else has had success doing so.

Overall, it was a fun puzzle to work on, despite the missing piece. I purchased another puzzle from the same manufacturer, but haven't put it together yet. If I have the same problems of uncut and missing pieces, I won't purchase anymore and certainly won't give one as a gift.

text_fidelity_a: Rodzon Remote RC Car，Control Truck with 2.4Ghz Controlled Toy Car for Kids & Adults，Double Sided 360° Flips. (No Battery Included) Green There is much to like about this cvar. It is sturdy and the bright green is sporty and attractive. It is fast and not obnoxiously noisy. It is responsive to the controls. It works best on flat, smooth surfaces. While it will run on lawns or carpets, and inclines, the smoother and flatter the surface the better. Now of r the negative. Batteries are not included, one of my pet peeves. When you get batteries to invest in rechargeables because this car and transmitter drain them fast. While the instruction do suggest turning both off when not in use they should highlight the consequences, to wit, extreme battery drain, if not followed. The controls are not intuitive. Once mastered they are okay but it takes some time and practice to get to that point. Still, it is fun for all ages and has thus far withstood some crashes without damage. It manoeuvres well and can do some pretty snazzy tricks.  Fast fun for all ages.

The eyes are painted on and don't look realistic to me, but at least nothing that can be broken or poked out. I was saying how fun it was and how these squishy toys are great for stress relief (which they are), and how it kind of smelled like vanilla or egg nog.  I thought it was such a cute little doll.  And I was going to mention that I still wouldn't let pets play with it since there were some tiny excess pieces at the seams that were coming loose.  And I started looking closer at the seam that extended all the way around the middle of the toy, as I lowered one of the arms to inspect the seam where the head and arm met, that area just started coming apart.  And it only took minimal pressure for it to continue to rip.  So then I looked at the same area where the head and shoulder/arm met on the other side, and the same thing happened. It just started coming apart.  You can see what I mean in the 4th and 5th photos.  This should not happen with any squishy toy, or any other toy for that matter.  I consider this a safety concern and am giving this toy one star for this reason.
text_fidelity_b: OYEFLY Squishy Toy Soft Exquisite Horror Doll Scented Stress Relief Toy Soft Toy Kawaii Collection Slow Rising Toy Decompression SimulationToys Cure Toy for Kid Gift Toys

BUNMO Infinity Cube Fidget Toy 2pk | Stimulating & Engaging Fidget Toy | Teen Boy Toys | Fidgets for Adults | Travel Toys | Gifts for Teenage Boys | 10 Year Old Boy Gift Ideas | Fidget Cube for Adults I've seen the plastic versions and heard that metal ones exist... but a wooden one? I had to try this one out.

If you've never used an infinity cube before, they're the latest in fun fidgety-toy types of thing, but also kind of more interesting because they bend and fold in ways that feel like it is constantly turning into something else. Sort like a transformer toy that goes on forever.

I really like the wood color and style of this, but my first impression wasn't very good. It was a lot harder to move and the wooden blocks would get stuck on each other as you bend and fold. Not anywhere near as smooth as the plastic variants. But the cords that hold this together just need some stretching to loosen them up. Once you've broken it in, it moves much more smoothly and eventually will give you the satisfying feel that an infinity cube is known for. I can't speak for the longevity of it yet, I am a little concerned that in the same way you need to break this in, it can also eventually stretch out and/or snap. But so far it's holding up and by then, I'm guessing a new fidget toy will be the latest craze.
text_fidelity_b: BUNMO Infinity Cube Fidget Toy 2pk | Stimulating & Engaging Fidget Toy | Teen Boy Toys | Fidgets for Adults | Travel Toys | Gifts for Teenage Boys | 10 Year Old Boy Gift Ideas | Fidget Cube for Adults

text_fidelity_a: Magicfly Bingo Daubers, Washable Dot Markers, 8 Colors Non-Toxic Paint Daubers, Water-Based Dauber Markers These are the first dot markers my 3.5 year old and I have tried. She is really enjoying them, but they don’t work quite like I imagined or hoped. First, card stock or thick paper seems ideal for not letting the color bleed through, but since I didn’t have any on hand I had to stack 3 pieces of normal paper to keep the color off our table. Second, they take awhile to prime. Even a couple minutes of unuse will require you to hold the marker down extra long to get the ink back in the tip. Third, even after priming you cannot move quickly with these markers - you really need to patiently, slowly, and evenly push down each dot to get a full circle. Many of my daughters dots are incomplete and even when I tried I couldn’t consistently get a complete dot. Also some colors seem to work better than others. Overall my daughter still likes them, but I cannot see her using them that often or being pleased with the results as she gets older.

I had to put on gloves to get a good grip to push the pins into the planets. Some of them, you hear a click, and some of them, you get no clicks no matter how hard you push.

3. The center projector that projects each planet is TERRIBLE. You need all the lights off, and you need the whole system to be close to the ceiling for you to see what planet its projecting. Out of focused and blurry. No way to focus it. The only way to get a sharper image is to put the project as close as possible to the wall.

4. Though the arms rotate around the sun, the individual planets do not rotate. So to explain night and day to your child, you'll need to manually rotate Earth. That would be asking too much, but hey, I thought this retails for $99? If they did charge $99, those planets better rotate by themselves. LOL!

3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Playz Premium Solar System Model Kit for Kids - 4 Speed Motor, HD Planetarium Projector, 8 Painted Planets & 8 White Foam Balls with Paint and Brush for a Hands-On STEM DIY Project for Space Toys

You see they have to view an app, which shows a speedometer. They need to keep the needle at a certain speed. Speedometer graphics is broken down into 2 colors, blue and red. If you go to the red, chances are good your car will fly off the tracks. How do you control the speed? By pumping the booster. The faster you pump, the needle will move towards the red. This comes with great directions, so you're led through what you need to do. You can order ants, but the directions are clear for if you chose to collect your own. The kit comes with a coupon to get cheaper ants. (I can't imagine anyone wanting ants bad enough to pay almost $20 for them.) The coupon and the first order page on the website says you'll get 5-10 ants, but then the main page says 30. Even with the coupon code, you're still paying $9.95 for ants(shipping IS included in that price). I can't pay that much when ants are in such abundance around our home. Again, though, I DO give them credit for the great directions for just using ants from the yard. You aren't expected to buy the ants, but you do have that option. Also, to make it clear, you won't get a queen ant if you order. You'll only get non-reproductive ants. (That information is from the website page for ordering the ants.)

It only took my boys a few minutes to come running with more than enough ants to fill their new little home. Unfortunately, our ants have been very slow to feel at home. One died, though we followed directions exactly. They aren't working together like I thought they would, either. That said, so far it has been greatly exciting to watch what little they have done. One ant looks like Goliath upside the other ants, so he's been easier to watch. It's surprisingly fascinating to watch ants move sand around! I assume there will be more efforts from the other ants with time, but I was expecting quicker results. (I don't blame that on the ant farm, by any means!)

One other complaint is the fact that the bottom goes on so loosely. I kept working with it thinking it should be tighter, but had no luck. This is something that will be best watched without too much handling from children, since there are 4 pieces that are easily removed. This kit comes with a tube, which can connect to another tree house if you chose to buy more. (The 2 side pieces can be removed for this connection.)

Overall, this is a fun kit for kids, but it could have been better designed. Every child needs to have the joy of watching ants work, though! ;)

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Definitely an enjoyable set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset

SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for $80.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is large enough to make it feel like a nice machine, but small enough, especially when folded, to port around, which is nice because it lends itself to easy travel. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards seemed kind of flimsy, and didn’t stay on well, so I flew without them. The drone handled test crashes well. The propellers held up well, with only some minor scrapes after hitting the ground and nearby trees. The copter simply hit the ground and the arms folded in on impact.

Quiet - The drone has a relatively quiet sound, and isn't too loud. I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. When executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward or backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button at the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Tuning - This was easy to do, and I liked the tactility of the joystick buttons. I found it worked well.

Camera usability- The quality is good, and it is fun to use. However, I’m kind of in the middle on this, which is why the camera is in both the pros and cons. It does provide an accurate view of what the drone sees, and I didn’t have almost any lag. The picture resolution was nice. It’s not super easy to use, but I was able to figure out most of the controls while flying.

Battery: This had a nice battery life, with about 22 minutes of battery life to 1.5 hours charging time. I didn’t stream video, which I would imagine uses a bit more battery, bt for my medium intensity flight, I was very happy with the flight time, especially considering that they give you two batteries, which could give you about 45 minutes of flight time.

Cons:
Unstable/Jerky Camera - Because the camera is hard-mounted to the drone body, the video is very twitchy and jerky as the drone flies around and tilts, particularly when descending. The video became very shaky. I found myself more inclined to use the photo option over the video though, because of how unstable it was. I also found the field of view to be frustratingly narrow, and wanted a more upwards view from the drone.

Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as set up the camera, one of the main selling points with this drone. I’ve found this is a common issue with Syma instructions, and it just makes the products a lot harder to use. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries

NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod My boys(5, 7, and 10) love Nerf guns. It's been a main request for birthdays and Christmas over the past year. For my 10 year old's last birthday, he requested a Nerf war. It was beyond fun to see the adults(of all ages) getting in on the fun right alongside the children. This one has a cool factor, since it's the longest Nerf gun at the moment and it truly is Mega. You can slide the barrel out to make it longer and slide it back in to make it shorter. It also has a bipod.

On the negative side, it takes up a great deal of room. It's a bit of a pain with its size. It's also so big that it's hard for my boys to use. I tried to use it and it's even awkward for me. I'd recommend this gun more for teens and adults. The only way my boys are really able to use it is with the bipod. It is a bit easier in the shorter length, but it's still heavy and awkward.

It also takes larger bullets than the average Nerf gun. It's a pain to have to worry about buying 2 separate kinds of bullets. All the rest of what we have take the same ones, and it makes things simpler. This gun comes with 10, but my boys lose darts constantly. Many times we discover where they were after the lawnmower turns them to confetti. Prepare for an extra investment if you don't already have other Mega guns.

Overall, if you don't mind buying the bigger bullets that go with this one and you or your child can handle the size, it's a pretty cool gun. My boys have had a hard time overly enjoying it, though, even if they do find it cool.
text_fidelity_b: NERF Thunderhawk Nerf AccuStrike Mega Toy Blaster - Longest Nerf Blaster - 10 Official AccuStrike Nerf Mega Darts, 10-Dart Clip, Bipod
